proposed_widenings.name: persistent_container_item_mechanics
proposed_widenings.justification: The item's main behavior is not a passive bonus, a one-shot activation, or a reaction. It is a persistent item-owned container with larger-on-the-inside storage semantics, capacity limits, retrieval interaction cost, usability state, and shared breathable-air tracking for creatures inside.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This bag has an interior space considerably larger than its outside dimensions... The bag can hold up to 500 pounds, not exceeding a volume of 64 cubic feet... Retrieving an item from the bag requires a Utilize action... The bag holds enough air for 10 minutes of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.

proposed_widenings.name: extradimensional_collision_and_rupture_hazard
proposed_widenings.justification: The bag has deterministic item-interaction and destruction behavior that depends on overload, damage state, inversion, and insertion into another extradimensional space. The current magic-item families cannot represent item-to-item collision rules, generated gate state, area suction, or forced planar relocation.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If the bag is overloaded, pierced, or torn, it is destroyed, and its contents are scattered in the Astral Plane... Placing a Bag of Holding inside an extradimensional space created by a Handy Haversack, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. Any creature within a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on the gate is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane.

notes: No Dhall/JSON encoding was authored. The existing magic-item surface only supports passive grants, bounded activations, triggered reactions, and composites of those. Bag of Holding's primary mechanic is durable container state plus a special extradimensional interaction hazard. The random Astral landing spot and the scope of "similar item" are caller/DM-owned details, but the unit is not overall dm_agenda because its destruction, gate opening, area pull, and planar exile are deterministic core mechanics.
